headline: Chromosome-level assemblies resolve polyploid origins and karyotype evolution in plants
label: Plant Genome Assemblies And Evolution
summary: Recent chromosome-level and haplotype-resolved assemblies now link genome structure to polyploid history and trait-relevant variation.
synthesis: The dominant thread is genome-resolved analysis of plant lineages, in which chromosome-level or haplotype-resolved assemblies reconstruct evolutionary history and locate trait-relevant variation. The wheatgrass assemblies resolve H and St subgenome origins, a stepwise polyploid history, and biased subgenome dominance. The sesame study reports karyotype evolution and a hybrid origin for S. radiatum across wild Sesamum and Ceratotheca species. The Madhuca hainanensis assembly (760.86 Mb) pairs comparative genomics with floral divergence, flagging six genes including ADO1 and COL5. The Aceraceae pan-genome links ActKCS to nervonic acid through GWAS and structural variants. The sorghum-anchored pan-grass syntenic gene set addresses orthologous and homeologous relationships among grass genes. The soybean GmHapMap-II resource is a population haplotype map rather than an assembly, linking 1,278 accessions to crude protein QTL and CNV at rhg-1/Rhg-4. What is new is the pairing of assembly-level structure with trait-level mapping, as in the Aceraceae and soybean studies.
